title: sharkd: Only peers with the same eUID may connect to Linux abstract sockets
description:
When listening on an abstract Unix domain socket, use SO_PEERCRED if we
have it to ensure that the peer process that connects has the same eUID
as the sharkd daemon.

Fix #21219

AI-Assisted: no

changes_data.diff:
@@ -67,14 +67,15 @@ Supported socket types:
 *unix:__path__*::
 Listen on a Unix domain socket at __path__.  For example,
 *unix:/tmp/sharkd.sock*.  On Linux, abstract sockets are supported
-by prefixing the name with *@*, for example *unix:@sharkd*.
+by prefixing the name with *@*, for example *unix:@sharkd*; abstract
+sockets only support connections from peers with the same effective UID.
 Unix domain sockets are available on Windows 10 version 1803 and
 later, including Windows Server 2019.
 
 *tcp:__address__:__port__*::
 Listen on a TCP socket bound to __address__ on __port__.  For example,
 *tcp:127.0.0.1:4446*.  For IPv6 addreses, enclose the address in square
-brackets, e.g. *tcp:[[::1]:5678*.  For security reasons,TCP sockets are
+brackets, e.g. *tcp:[[::1]:5678*.  For security reasons, TCP sockets are
 only available on Windows builds by default and only loopback addresses
 are supported, i.e. an IPv4 address in the *127.0.0.0/8* address space
 or the *::1* IPv6 loopback address.

@@ -136,8 +136,10 @@ The following features are either new or have been significantly updated since v
 Dumpcap's TCP@host:port interface has been removed.
 
 Sharkd only supports binding to a loopback IPv4 or IPv6 address when listening
-on a TCP socket. (TCP sockets are only available when UNIX domain sockets are
-unsupported. IPv6 support is new.)
+on a TCP socket. (TCP sockets are only available by default on Windows systems,
+and are deprecated, since UNIX domain sockets are now supported. IPv6 support
+is new.) Sharkd now rejects connecting to a Linux abstract domain socket from
+peer processes with effective UID other than that of the sharkd process.
 
 The individual color preferences under menu:Appearance[] (marked and ignored packets, "Follow Stream" client and server text, display filter validity, and the selected packet) have been removed. These colors are now provided by the selected theme; see the "What's New" section above.

+/**
+ * @brief Verify the credentials of the peer connected to a Unix domain socket

+ * Verifies that the UID of the peer process that is connected to a Unix domain socket

+ * @param sock A socket handle (on UN*X, file descriptor)
+ * @return true on success, or false on failure (including if unsupported).
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC bool ws_verify_peercred(socket_handle_t sock);
+
